origins.base layer: Essential packages of the pinned Debian trixie-slim base (glibc, util-linux, ncurses, acl, zlib, perl-base), which the image cannot drop. Debian publishes no fixed package in trixie or trixie-security for any of them (Grype fix state wont-fix or not-fixed), so under H9 no fix is available. The local privilege-escalation findings (util-linux mount helpers, nsenter, restricted bind mounts; acl TOCTOU and symlink traversal) need a privileged process to subvert, and there is none: the agent runs unprivileged with every capability dropped, no-new-privileges, and no setuid or setgid file in the image (research R7, SC-4). The rest are memory or resource bugs in library calls and tools (strfmon, ns_printrr, infocmp, gzwrite, Pod::Text, Archive::Tar) reached only when the agent itself runs them, inside its own container.
origins.files under /opt/agent: The agent runtimes added by discovery revision 14 (feature 007 slice 1): the agent Python (uv-managed CPython with its bundled pip) and Node (the official tarball, with npm and npm's bundled dependencies), under /opt/agent. Nothing in timelike runs them: the agent runs them itself, unprivileged, inside its own container. Under H9 a finding here is accepted only when no fix is available at all; a fix in a later release of the package is never baselined, even while no Node or npm release ships it (the gate blocks it). Each entry has its own reason below.
origins.git: Pulled in by git (libcurl3t64-gnutls, libexpat1, perl, libperl5.40, perl-modules-5.40). git stays: https fetch is essential to P1 (stack note 15). Debian publishes no fixed package in trixie or trixie-security (Grype: wont-fix or not-fixed). The libcurl Highs need features git's https transport does not use or the image does not configure: SFTP/SCP, LDAP SASL, STARTTLS, cookies (no http.cookieFile), public-key pinning with verification off, mTLS option changes, HTTP/3, pause callbacks in the multi socket API. libexpat is used by git only for http-push (WebDAV), which timelike does not use. The perl module findings are reached only when the agent runs those modules itself. The agent holds no credentials in slice 0 (P4), which bounds every credential-reuse class. Each Critical has its own reason below.

findings.reason: Use-after-free that needs CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS followed by curl_easy_reset. git's http transport never sets HTTP/2 stream dependencies.

Digest Authorization header carried to a second origin on a reused handle. The agent holds no credentials in slice 0 (P4): no credential helper, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, empty askpass, so no Authorization header exists to leak. Re-review when Adele (feature 12) brokers credentials.
Use-after-free in HTTP/2 server push with shared connections. Server push needs a push callback (CURLMOPT_PUSHFUNCTION), which git's http transport does not set.

Negotiate (SPNEGO) connection reuse after an empty-credential request. The image has no Kerberos credentials and sets no http.emptyAuth, and the agent holds no credentials at all (P4), so there is no authenticated connection for another request to ride on. Re-review when Adele (feature 12) brokers credentials.
Cookie Public Suffix List bypass. git reads and sends cookies only when http.cookieFile is set, and nothing in the image sets it.
Wrong .netrc password for a URL with a username. The image ships no .netrc and the agent holds no credentials to put in one (P4). Re-review when Adele (feature 12) brokers credentials.
Proxy Digest state kept across environment-variable proxies. The image sets no proxy variables and no proxy credentials. Re-review if an egress proxy is introduced (Adele, feature 12).
Proxy credentials not cleared between transfers. The image configures no proxy and no proxy credentials, and the agent holds none (P4). Re-review if an egress proxy is introduced (Adele, feature 12).

libexpat1 2.8.3-1~deb13u1 (CVE-2026-77214): heap over-read in XML_ParseBuffer with a caller-supplied length. No Debian fix (Grype: not-fixed). Pulled in by git, which uses expat only for http-push over WebDAV, which timelike does not use. Not caused by 007 slice 1: it is in the base layer's git and would block master too. Revisit when Debian ships a fix.

npm's bundled http-cache-semantics 4.2.0 (GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp, alias CVE-2026-93748): max-stale handling can serve a cached response across users. No fixed release exists. In npm it decides freshness for npm's own registry cache, which here is per user (~/.npm of the one agent user) and holds public package metadata: there is no second user whose responses could be disclosed. Revisit when a fixed release ships in npm.
